commits.author: mohammedwessam2007
commits.message:
Build the six computable frontier artifacts, and split what is left from them (#938)

* Build the six computable frontier artifacts, and split what is left from them

Finishes every contract artifact this repository can honestly produce: baselines,
evaluation epoch, mission DAG, resource allocation, frontier checkpoint, final
frontier state. They are one generator because they are one computation read six
ways -- the checkpoint is the DAG plus the baselines, the allocation is the DAG
filtered, the final state is all of it plus the completion law. Six generators
would mean six reads of the same inputs and six chances to disagree about which
head they describe.

The baselines found something on their first run. artifacts/system-readiness.json
records 871 files parsed; the tree parses 2,189. It records 3,683 deterministic
tests with 3 failures; the tree runs over 7,700 with none, and 168 mutations
against 502 registered guards. Every one of those was written down in good faith
at a moment when it was true. What makes them dangerous is that they read
exactly like a measurement taken now.

So a number's provenance travels with the number. LIVE was measured by the run
that produced the artifact; RECORDED was copied from something somebody else
wrote down, and carries its age. A recorded figure with no timestamp is stale
rather than fresh, because currency can never be established for it at all --
defaulting it to fresh would make the least trustworthy figure in the file look
like the best one. Where a live and a recorded value disagree, the disagreement
is listed and neither is edited: overwriting the record destroys the evidence
that it drifted, and averaging them produces a number describing no tree.

The allocator deliberately does not rank by expected value. No economic prior
exists for any of this work and inventing one would dress a guess as arithmetic.
It allocates across missions that are actionable now and lists the rest with what
they wait on, because a dependency is ours to clear and an external blocker is
not -- conflating them turns a waiting list into a to-do list nobody can finish.

The epoch refuses to claim a trend. One epoch is FIRST_EPOCH__NO_COMPARISON_
POSSIBLE and two are CHANGE_MEASURED__TOO_FEW_EPOCHS_FOR_A_TREND, because a
delta between two points is a difference, not a direction.

With those six written, no absent contract artifact is computable any more, so
V7G009 closes on computable work rather than on total absence, and the eleven
that remain move to V7G010 as external. That is the same split already applied
to the deployment gap, and the absence reasons it rests on were classified before
any of these were built.

Also repairs V7G005. It counted commits ahead of main and reported "nothing
stranded" while this very check sat uncommitted in the working tree. Uncommitted
work is stranded in the most literal sense: it exists on one disk and nowhere
else.

11 tests. 6 mutation guards, all killed.

Separate proof debt from rules no guard can settle, and bind claims to heads (#928)

* Separate proof debt from rules no guard can settle, and bind claims to heads

PHASE 3. Both artifacts exist to stop a number meaning less than it looks like.

The doctor's "unguarded external-effect directives" mixed two things. A
prohibition on an external effect can be settled by removing the protection and
watching a test go red. A permission cannot be settled that way by anyone,
because granting latitude has no failure state to catch. Counting them together
produced a review queue that read as a defect list, and reading all 22 by hand
was the only way to tell which was which.

Now it is computed. Of 262 directives: 43 are not dischargeable by code at all,
177 want an ordinary test, 31 want a mutation guard, 11 want an executable
check. The number worth acting on is 14 -- rules code could settle that it has
not. That is a smaller and truer figure than 19 unguarded, and it is the first
one that is actually a work queue.

The obligation kinds are ordered most-demanding-first, because an external-effect
prohibition also matches the weaker INTERNAL_TEST rule and filing it there would
let a test that merely mentions the subject discharge it. A mention is not
enforcement; that distinction is what the whole constitution effort turns on.

The claim-evidence registry asks a different question: this repository asserts
things about itself -- softwareOpen is 1, 490 mutations killed, canonical V9 not
materialized -- and each was true of some tree at some moment. Nothing checked
whether that moment is this one. It has already gone wrong twice here: a
constitution artifact merged claiming 464 anchors against a tree holding 469,
and a readiness artifact described a commit whose source had since changed.

Running it immediately flagged four stale claims from artifacts generated before
the last squash merge. Regenerating cleared them, which is the check working
rather than a coincidence. Evidence with no head reads NOT_HEAD_BOUND rather
than fresh, because a health probe is timed and not committed, and reading it as
exact-head would make an observation from hours ago look like it was taken at
this commit.

One finding from building it: the canonical-V9 claim originally cited the blocker
document, which records one investigation and goes stale by design. It now cites
the gap ledger, which re-runs the materializer at whatever head it reports. A
claim should point at the thing that re-measures it.

Also classifies the remaining absent artifacts. Seventeen absent was not
actionable; the reason each is absent is. Six are COMPUTABLE_NOW -- ordinary
work waiting to be done. Eleven wait on something no amount of writing produces:
repeated observation, elapsed time, external reality, or a lattice runtime that
does not exist. Writing a status file for a runtime that does not exist would be
precisely the confusion the doctrine names. An absence with no reason is now
reported as a defect in the index, which is how the last one was caught.

11 tests. 6 mutation guards, all killed.

* Make claim staleness about source, not about the head moving

My own test caught this one. Comparing a claim's recorded head against current
HEAD is unsatisfiable: committing the artifact changes HEAD, so a registry
generated immediately before a commit is stale the moment it lands. Every commit
would have produced a red gate, and a staleness signal that fires on everything
trains a reader to ignore the word.

The question that actually matters is the one canon-freshness already asks: has
any source the claim depends on changed since it was measured? An artifact
naming the parent commit with nothing but regenerated artifacts after it is
still describing this tree. So the range is diffed and filtered to
src/scripts/config/migrations/tests, and a stale claim now names the files that
falsified it rather than only asserting it is old.

An unreadable commit range is handled separately and is worse than stale: a
recorded head that cannot be found is a claim whose basis has been rewritten or
lives on another branch, and reporting that as "no changes" would be the exact
inversion.

Turn a real health probe into evidence, and stop the ledger reading complete (#923)

* Turn a real health probe into evidence, and stop the ledger reading complete

Two ends existed and nothing joined them. waitForUberLitHealth probes a running
service and returns a status; the Ubercel doctor reads contract-bound
AUTHENTICATED_HEALTH signals and reports SERVING or NOT_SERVING from them.
Between the two there was nothing -- so a real probe, /api/health returning 200
against the live Render deployment, was written into a handoff document as a
sentence, and the doctor went on reporting UNKNOWN__ONLY_PROVIDER_BADGES.
Prose is not a signal.

That probe is now recorded with its actual provenance: observed at
2026-09-17T16:46:59.098Z by the deployment session that landed 9df093b2, not by
this one. The doctor consequently reports UNKNOWN__EVIDENCE_STALE. That is the
honest answer and the point of the distinction: we knew the service was healthy
at 16:46, and we do not know it now. "We have no way to know" and "we knew, and
the knowledge expired" are different problems, and only the second is waiting on
time.

What the bridge refuses matters as much as what it does. It never probes, so
running it cannot manufacture the evidence it records -- a test replaces global
fetch with a throw to hold that. A 200 from a URL nobody declared is recorded
and binds to nothing. The right URL with the wrong status does not bind either.
An observation with no observer is refused, because a probe with no observer
cannot later be told apart from one this repository invented; an observation
with no readable time is refused, because it could never be aged and so could
never be known stale.

Closing V7G003's software half moved softwareOpen to 0 and the ledger to
sourceSideComplete: true -- which was false. Nineteen artifacts the contract
names do not exist, and a ledger with no row for them is not a ledger that
found nothing. V7G009 counts them from the index, which reads statSync rather
than intent, so an empty file cannot close it. softwareOpen is 1 again and
sourceSideComplete is false, which is the true state.

The five external gaps are genuinely external: canonical V9's missing bytes, the
founder precedence decision, a fresh authorized probe, no cleared payment, no
configured provider.

11 tests. 6 mutation guards, all killed.

V9 carrier repair, and the V7 gap ledger computed from source (#922)

* Repair 14 V9 seed parts, and name the one byte-range nobody has

CLAUDE_START_V9.md requires LOSSLESS_VERIFIED and SHA-256 8ad73f53...e55d
before canonical V9 may be treated as canonical. The carrier in this repository
cannot produce it, and this establishes exactly why rather than leaving the next
session to rediscover it.

The materializer reported SEED_ENCODED_PART_MISMATCH:part-0001.xz.b64 and
stopped. That reads as total corruption. It was not. Fifteen of sixteen seed
parts were each exactly one byte short -- a stripped trailing newline -- and
restoring it makes every one of their encoded SHA-256 hashes match the manifest
exactly. Fourteen are repaired here; part 7 had been repaired already in
8daf918a, which is why it alone verified.

Part 16 is different. It is 6,500 bytes where the manifest requires 12,933,
short 4,823 binary bytes of LZMA-compressed V7 content. That is not a checksum
and nothing in this repository can recompute it. Six mechanisms were tested and
all failed with certain outcomes: both sibling carrier branches carry the same
truncation or commit no parts at all; all 36,521 git objects were scanned by
size and none matches V7's 1,916,551 bytes; the alternate Brotli carrier
declares 128 parts and holds 2; no large blob resembles V7, V8 or V9; and the
generator is intact but forward-only and refuses any seed whose xz hash differs.
The truncated stream still decodes 96.3% of V7 before simply ending, mid-sentence
at directive 1510 -- the remainder is absent, not damaged.

Wallbreaker receipt wbr_c63017e3fd1a01caec01828a selected external-source
acquisition and ruled two candidates ineligible by hard constraint:
brute-forcing the missing bytes (no-fabricated-bytes) and editing the manifest
so the short carrier passes (no-manifest-hash-weakening). Those are the two
shapes this failure invites, and both are refused in code, not just in prose.

The verifier is unweakened. LOSSLESS_VERIFIED still requires every hash. What
changed is the failure path: it now checks all sixteen parts before reporting,
separates a part repairable without any source from one that is not, and names
the artifact and hash that would close it. A verifier that stops at the first
symptom hides the shape of the damage, and the shape is the part a human can act
on.

Also repairs the harness that was supposed to guard this. Mutation-war validated
every mutant with `node --check`, so a mutation of any .py file reported
MUTANT_DID_NOT_PARSE however well-formed it was -- meaning no Python in this
repository could ever be guarded, including the one script standing between a
partial carrier and a hash-locked artifact. The checker now follows the
language. Verified not to regress JS mutants.

7 tests. 3 mutation guards, all killed: a truncated part classified as
newline-repairable, a broken carrier proceeding to generation, and the refusal
reporting one part when sixteen were checked.

Canonical V9 remains unmaterialized. The blocker is recorded at
artifacts/v9/canonical-v9-materialization-blocker.json with the exact bytes
required and who can supply them.

* Compute the V7 gap ledger, and map the contract's artifacts to what exists

PHASE 0 and PHASE 1 of the execution order, from the recoverable V7 ancestor.
Canonical V9 is still unmaterialized, so this executes from V7 and every
artifact says so in the field rather than in a footnote: executedFrom reads
PARTIAL_V7_ANCESTOR__EXPLICITLY_NOT_CANONICAL_V9.

The gap ledger's contract is three sentences and all three are about the same
failure: a label never closes a gap, a stale artifact never closes a gap, a
self-authored claim never closes an external gap. So no gap here carries a
writable status. Each owns a check that runs the materializer, a doctor, a
ratchet, or git, and the status is whatever that check returned at the head it
ran against. Editing the artifact closes nothing.

Three refusals fall out of that and each is guarded. A check that throws records
CHECK_FAILED rather than collapsing into OPEN or CLOSED, because "we looked and
it is fine" and "we could not look" are different facts. A gap claiming an
external blocker without naming what would unblock it falls back to OPEN --
"EXTERNAL_BLOCKED, reason: pending" is precisely the label the contract forbids.
And source-side completion requires zero unmeasured gaps as well as zero open
ones, or a broken check becomes a way to finish.

Current measured state: 8 gaps, 2 software-open, 4 external, 0 unmeasured.
The two open are the deployment health contract and this branch's own unmerged
commits. The four external are canonical V9's missing bytes, no cleared payment,
no configured provider, and the founder precedence decision.

The artifact index resolves the tension in the contract's own wording: it names
29 machine-readable artifacts and also says to reuse existing source where
equivalent capability exists. Generating 29 files would produce mostly stubs and
bury the few carrying real measurement; generating some would silently drop the
rest. So each name resolves to GENERATED, COVERED_BY_EXISTING_ARTIFACT with what
that cover actually holds, or ABSENT -- and ABSENT stays counted. Nineteen are
absent. An artifact nobody has is a gap, and it is worth more visible than
papered over with an empty file. Verified against the contract text: 29
declared, 29 mapped, none dropped.

Also fixes a bug found by running it: the live-truth generator discarded the V9
materializer's report because the materializer exits non-zero by design, so the
field read UNOBSERVED when the script had just taken the trouble to explain
itself.

commits.message:
Read deployment state through Ubercel instead of off a vendor's badge (#919)

* Read deployment state through Ubercel instead of off a vendor's badge

Ubercel already existed, and I misreported it. src/ubercel-deployment-control-plane.mjs
treats VERCEL as one of five replaceable adapter types, refuses any adapter that
declares deploymentAuthority, and carries the law NO_PROVIDER_IS_THE_CONTROL_PLANE.
A session then read a red Vercel commit status and reported it as UberBond's
deployment truth, in a PR comment and twice in a PR body.

The law was enforced at plan time and nowhere at read time, because nothing
answered "what is our deployment state?" at all. Ubercel could compile a plan
and a failover; it could not be asked what was true now. So the only readable
thing was a vendor badge, and that is what got read.

The distinction this adds: a provider badge is a fact about the provider. It
becomes a fact about UberBond only if UberBond serves from it, which is a
question the badge cannot answer about itself. Only a probe bound to the health
contract UberBond declared, or liveness from a runtime UberBond owns, describes
UberBond.

So a red badge alone reports UNKNOWN__ONLY_PROVIDER_BADGES rather than
NOT_SERVING -- a vendor build failing may be a surface we do not serve from --
and a green badge alone reports the same, which is the more dangerous error in
the other direction and the one a passing build invites.

npm run ubercel:doctor, against the signals as actually observed:

  state: UNKNOWN__ONLY_PROVIDER_BADGES
  contract-bound authoritative signals: 0
  provider badges (each establishes nothing about UberBond):
    vercel [VERCEL] serving=false
    vercel-lite-private [VERCEL] serving=false

That is the honest current state. Nothing in this repository collects
contract-bound health evidence yet, and the doctor says so rather than letting
an absence read as health.

The module is wired to a script rather than classified in the reachability
config, for the reason that config gives: a module reachable only from tests is
not reachable.

13 tests. 5 mutation guards, all killed: a badge establishing serving state, an
authenticated probe counting while unbound from the declared contract, stale and
future-dated evidence counting as current, an adapter promoting its own
evidence, and one authenticated not-serving being outvoted by healthy ones.

On the other named layers: uberagents, uberdistribution, ubereconomy, ubermodels,
uberpay and ubervault have no uber-named module, but each has substantial
capability under its existing name -- 21, 8, 16, 10, 14 and 3 modules
respectively. Those are naming gaps, not capability gaps, and creating uber-named
duplicates of agent-mesh-*, distribution-*, economic-*, agent-model-*, billing-*
and secret-* would be the capability sprawl the canon prohibits. Left alone
deliberately.

The compiler's source list carried the comment "Canon files, in precedence
order. NORTH_STAR.md and the precedence file define that order." That was false
twice over: docs/NORTH_STAR_PRECEDENCE.md ranks ten files and exactly one of
them is in the list, and every compiled directive carried priority: 0, so no
order was applied even within it.

Fixing it turned up two facts worth having.

The precedence law cannot settle any conflict between operative rules. It ranks
ten files, nine of which are the terminal North Star layer. The files that
actually bind an agent -- AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, UBERBOND_CANON.md and the
docs/*_CANON.md set -- carry no relative rank anywhere, so 0 of the 9 detected
conflict candidates have an authored answer. One of them is live: the Wallbreaker
canon prohibits evading provider limits while CLAUDE.md permits automatic
failover, and nothing in the repository says which governs.

That is not mine to answer. Ranking one canon file above another decides which
rule wins in a real conflict, which is an amendment, and F003 says founder
sovereignty rules are not autonomously modifiable. So precedenceFor returns
precedenceRank: null with state UNRANKED__NO_AUTHORED_PRECEDENCE -- the old
priority: 0 read as *highest* precedence, which is the opposite of the truth --
and resolveByPrecedence refuses any pair with an unranked side and names the
source that needs a rank. The question is recorded as FD002 in
artifacts/constitution/open-founder-decisions.json with the three options and
the note that ranking the operative canon in the precedence file resolves the
graph with no code change, because the ranks are parsed from that file rather
than transcribed.

The terminal layer's absence is now declared rather than merely true. Those nine
files hold 886 normative sentences and compiling them would take the constitution
from 262 directives to about 1148, nearly all of them arriving as rules awaiting
a guard. NORTH_STAR.md states their status plainly -- "direction and search-space
canon, not implementation proof" -- and a Directive Object asserts
REPOSITORY_TEST_OR_EXECUTABLE_CHECK, so compiling them would make the opposite
claim about all 886 and bury the 48 external-effect rules that bind behaviour
today. TERMINAL_SOURCES names them with that reason, and a test fails if a
ranked file is ever neither compiled nor declared excluded, which is the
silent-drop case the no-amputation law exists to prevent.

commits.message:
Fix the scheduler test's teardown race, and correct my first diagnosis of it

This test failed intermittently in the full suite and never in isolation, and
the first thing I changed was its wait budget. That was wrong and the code now
says so rather than carrying a confident wrong comment.

The real error is ENOTEMPTY, thirty milliseconds in. The predicate is satisfied
almost immediately, stop() is called, and the fixture directory is deleted while
work is still landing in it. stop() clears the interval timers and returns
synchronously -- it does not await the promises already in flight, and with a
one-second wealth heartbeat and a dozen jobs firing their first tick
immediately, several are mid-write when it returns.

That is a reasonable scheduler design. A caller wanting quiescence should wait
for it, and the test was not. Under parallel load the window widens, which is
why the full suite exposed it and isolation never did.

Teardown now retries on ENOTEMPTY and EBUSY while the work settles, and rethrows
anything else rather than swallowing a real failure. Reproduced under artificial
load before the fix and passing three for three under the same load after.

The wait budget stays raised -- a one-second bound is a race against machine
load either way -- but its comment no longer claims to have fixed something it
did not.

No production code changed. The race was in the test.

Final report, computed rather than written

A summary is the easiest place in a project to lie, because nothing checks it.
So the generation table is read from the result files, capability is measured
live at report time, and the verdict is the completion ledger's own count rather
than a sentence. Nine tests hold it, including that it regenerates to the same
figures and that its verdict matches the ledger.

  SOFTWARE_SIDE_COMPLETE -- 0 software items open, 2 external
  8 generations, 6 promoted, 2 null results
  12 failure-debt entries, all closed with a regression test and a commit
  headroom remaining at tool use and forecasting, difficulties 4 and 5

The central finding, which cost five generations to learn properly: an
evaluation drawn from inside the distribution a solver was built against cannot
tell a mechanism from a lookup over that distribution. A tournament can be run
carefully -- thresholds fixed beforehand, held-out seeds, null candidates,
regression checks -- and still promote something that memorised the shape of the
questions. The tournament is not where the defect lives.

Both corrections that went against me are in the report and in the summary: the
cross-organ task whose first construction was unanswerable and flattered the arm
under test, and the verdict that called an implementation transferable because
0.43 beat a rule scoring 0 by being systematically wrong. A test asserts both
are still there, because they are the two easiest things to quietly drop.

The report disclaims, explicitly and under test, general intelligence,
superintelligence, intelligence explosion, singularity and recursive
self-improvement. None of them is supported by anything here. Every solver is a
hand-written deterministic function, so what improved is an understanding of a
task expressed as code. Revenue, customers and cleared payment remain zero.

The GA2 declaration argued that ranking sources on provenance and freshness
should transfer to organs weighing evidence whose quality signals conflict.
That was an architectural argument and nothing measured it.

Receiving organ: the epistemic immune system, which carries its own evidence
vocabulary -- KNOWLEDGE_STATES, twelve states ordered weakest first -- sharing
no label with the suite the solver was built against. Strength is the position
in that ordering, so no arm can quietly disagree with the organ about what
counts as better evidence. Sixty constructed claims, truth planted before any
source is written, sources shuffled.

  MECHANISM_ON_ORGAN_VOCABULARY   60/60
  PROMOTED_SOLVER_UNCHANGED       26/60
  PRE_GA2_FLAT_LADDER              0/60

The promoted solver carries a table of the suite's own labels, so handed an
organ that names evidence differently it scores every source at zero and falls
through to whatever comes first. Two of four sources carry the truth, so that
lands at chance. The same rule reading the organ's ordering gets all sixty.

Two corrections along the way, both of which favoured the arm under test before
they were caught.

The first construction drew the truth-carrying sources from states 4 to 6 and
gave the decoy HYPOTHETICAL -- state 5 -- at the latest date. The decoy was as
strong as the truth and fresher, so no rule weighing strength against recency
could recover the intended answer. Every arm scored noise and the promoted
solver came out ahead at 0.48 by picking whatever the shuffle put first. It was
caught because the ordering of the arms made no sense, not because a check
failed. Its numbers are not reported: a measurement of an unanswerable question
is not a weaker measurement, it is not one.

The second was the verdict. It compared every arm against the pre-GA2 ladder
and concluded the implementation transferred, because 0.43 beats 0. But the
ladder scores 0 by being systematically wrong, and beating a systematically
wrong rule is not evidence. Against chance, the implementation does not
transfer. Chance is now the baseline and a test holds it there.

So "the solver transfers" is false, "nothing transfers" is false, and the true
statement is narrower than either: a mechanism transfers when given the
receiving organ's vocabulary, and an implementation carrying its own does not
travel with it. Which is the same finding as F010 in a different register --
vocabulary and reasoning are separable, and mistaking one for the other has now
cost two generations and one transfer claim.

The organ is unmodified. Transfer measured on constructed tasks is not transfer
to that organ's work, and a test asserts the organ does not reference the
instrument.

CD005 closes. softwareOpen is 0.

commits.message:
Treat a tie as unresolved rather than breaking it on bytes

Twice a tie-break decided which implementation ships on something carrying no
information about behaviour. GA6 chose L2 over L3 because L2 was smaller, and
L2 turned out to confabulate on every difficulty-4 item while L3 refused
cleanly -- found only once a level existed that could ask. GA7 chose M3 over M4
on registration order because neither size could be measured, and checking by
hand showed M4 silently drops trailing operations. Both times the tie meant the
instrument could not separate them, both times they were separable by evidence
nobody ran, and the second time it was luck that the better one won.

So before size or ordering decides anything, tied candidates are now run
against each other on the family's probe sets and on the generated items. If
they disagree anywhere they are not interchangeable, no tie-break the
tournament has can choose between them on evidence, and the outcome is
NO_PROMOTION__TIE_UNRESOLVED. If they agree everywhere measured, any of them
will do.

The rule lives in src/nullstar-tie-resolution.mjs rather than inline in the
runner, so it is testable with fixtures instead of only through a whole
generation.

Writing those tests found a defect underneath it. runProbes swallowed a thrown
solver into the same null a refusal produces, so a candidate crashing on every
probe was indistinguishable from one deliberately declining. That mattered
twice: the gate treats refusal as acceptable behaviour, so crashing passed the
same way, and a tie-break comparing two candidates read a crash as agreement
with a refusal. Throwing is now its own outcome and fails the gate outright at
any minimum -- refusing is a decision about the edge of competence, crashing is
the absence of one.

GA6 and GA7 stand as taken under the rules in force when they ran. GA7's
promotion happens to be right, and the only reason that is known is that it was
checked by hand afterwards, which was the problem.

CD008 and CD010 close. Two software items remain: the right-grouped
composition nothing measures, and cross-organ transfer.

Enumerate the probe grammar, and separate limitations from debt

CD003 said the probes were written by the same author as the solvers, so they
test the failure modes that author thought of. Two different claims were tangled
in that, one actionable and one not.

The actionable half: the gate rested on six hand-written prompts, so passing it
could mean those six happened to be six the solver could do. The invention
prompts come from a small grammar -- two of four quantities, one of five
operators, either order -- which is finite, so it is enumerable rather than
sampled. 54 prompts. The promoted solver answers all 54 with zero
confabulations. Six hand-picked cases are now a vanishing fraction of what it
was measured on.

The half that is not actionable: whoever writes the next probe set is an author
too. No work closes that. An item that can never close is a limitation filed as
debt, and leaving it in a ledger whose count decides whether work is finished
would make the count hostage to a truism -- it could never reach zero, so
reaching zero would stop meaning anything.

So the ledger now has a permanentLimitations section that does not enter the
count: probes and solvers share an author, every number comes from one
instrument, and the solvers are hand-written deterministic functions rather
than models, so what is being improved is the author's understanding of the
task expressed as code. All three are stated rather than narrowed away, and the
artifact says explicitly that reaching zero software items would not mean they
had gone away.

This is a reclassification and it is visible as one: the item keeps its number,
records what it was reclassified from, and the limitation it shed is written
down in full rather than dropped.

commits.author: Claude
commits.message:
Build an instrument that can be wrong, and find three defects in it

The retired corpus compared a tree to itself. These tasks are built the other
way round: a seeded generator constructs a structure and knows the answer by
construction, the solver sees only the surface, and the harness strips the item
before the call rather than trusting the solver not to look. Seven families,
all deterministic, all reproducible from a seed.

Writing the verification found three defects in my own generators, any one of
which would have shipped a lying instrument.

The xorshift PRNG returned a near-zero first value for every small seed, so
every generator's first decision was pinned: science drew the same hidden rule
every time and causality drew CHAIN for all eight seeds. Two of seven families
were measuring a constant. The seed is now mixed and the stream warmed before
anything is handed out.

The forecasting series drew a fresh step per element, producing [10,12,16,22,
22,25] and then extrapolating from a step that never existed. The item was
unanswerable rather than hard.

Research put the primary measurement first in every item, so a baseline that
took sources[0] scored a perfect 1.0 on the family without weighing anything.
Sources are shuffled, and the distinct-claim count went from two to five
because a two-way choice hands a coin flip half the item.

The ground truth of every family is confirmed against an independent
computation, not against the generator that produced it: planning's longest
chain is recomputed from the edge list by a different method, and the suite
fails if the two ever disagree.

Baselines v2 on 70 items: trivial 0.029, ancestor 0, current 1.0, margin 0.97.
The ancestor scores zero because it carries neither the generator nor the
solvers, so that delta is capability added rather than capability improved, and
the record says so.

B5 is at ceiling. A suite at ceiling registers neither improvement nor
regression, which is the exact condition that let the retired corpus sit at 1.0
for four generations, so difficulty has to rise before this can measure a
capability generation. The record also states the limitation a reader would
otherwise have to notice: these solvers were authored with knowledge of the
generators, so a ceiling score says the items are within reach of code written
alongside them, not that the system is generally capable.

commits.message:
NULLSTAR OMEGA spine: denominator, sealed holdouts, bottleneck engine, G0, G1

Archaeology first. The evaluation primitives already existed -- compound
intelligence evaluation, benchmark evidence ledger, cross-domain transfer,
the C21 evidence factory. What did not exist anywhere on disk was a single
generation artifact. The loop had never been run, which is exactly the
"infrastructure without a completed generation is insufficient" case.

THE DENOMINATOR (N01-N24)

States are computed from file evidence, never asserted, and the top two
rungs are unreachable from source: OPERATING needs a receipt a run
produced, REALITY_CALIBRATED needs a prediction later checked against an
observation. Writing more code cannot move a dimension past VERIFIED,
which is the difference between a system that could work and one that has.

Additive only. A compile that loses a dimension fails, checked against the
prior compile's ids -- a denominator you can shorten reports a better
number every time a hard dimension becomes inconvenient.

First compile named the minimum cut set without being told: N03
SEALED_HOLDOUTS, N04 BOTTLENECK_DISCOVERY, N10 IMPROVEMENT_VELOCITY were
the only ABSENT dimensions, and they are precisely the recursive spine.

WHAT WAS BUILT

Sealed holdouts store answers as digests salted per suite and task, so a
common answer is not matchable against a public corpus. Sealed tasks never
return plaintext, the committed manifest carries no prompts or answers,
and a sealed digest appearing in the visible corpus fails the compile
rather than being noticed later. Abstention scores apart from a wrong
answer, because collapsing them punishes calibrated refusal.

The bottleneck engine ranks by downstream unlocks per unit cost from a
declared dependency graph, so a diagnosis can be argued with by pointing
at the graph. Two hypotheses and a discriminating test are required: one
hypothesis is a guess wearing a ranking. Weak evidence is ranked but never
selected first -- a story about the system must not outrank a measured
failure of it.

Generations pin exact commit, suite and corpus. An unmeasured dimension is
null and never zero, and only dimensions measured in both generations are
compared -- counting a newly-measured dimension as a gain is the most
available way to manufacture improvement.

G0, THE BOTTLENECK, AND A REFUTED HYPOTHESIS

G0 measured 4 of 17 dimensions and scored 1.0 on all four. The engine
flagged the saturation itself: all 17 dimensions depend on evaluation, so
it carried the highest leverage in the graph. Its hypothesis was that the
tasks were too easy, each a direct read of a value an artifact states.

G1 ran the discriminating test. Nine dimensions, every answer derived
across artifacts rather than read -- and every score still 1.0.

The hypothesis is REFUTED. It is recorded in refutations.json and the
engine now refuses to re-select it, because re-running a falsified
candidate spends generations confirming what was already disproved.

The successor diagnosis is worse news and better science: every local task
is a deterministic assertion over repository artifacts, so it measures the
internal consistency the existing 6,900-test suite already enforces, not
capability. Separating them needs a judgement the repository does not
compute -- which needs a configured model provider. That is an external
gate, not a software gap, and no further corpus authorship closes it.

Denominator after the cycle: ABSENT 3 to 0, OPERATING 1 to 6, and
REALITY_CALIBRATED still 0 -- nothing here has yet predicted something and
been checked against reality. Velocity reports INSUFFICIENT_DATA because
two points are a line. Acceleration is NOT_ESTABLISHED.

Eight mutants killed across the four modules: removing a dimension,
reaching OPERATING from source alone, a sealed task returning its answer,
dropping the digest salt, accepting one hypothesis, letting weak evidence
rank first, defaulting an unmeasured dimension to zero, and calling a
trend from two points.

commits.author: Claude
commits.message:
Reduce the MISSING upper bound with reviewed aliases, not a looser matcher

253 sections read MISSING because the matcher will not split a title on
whitespace -- "GENESIS for Life" contains "GENESIS", and a looser join is
exactly how a coverage report becomes fiction. That understates coverage,
which is the safe direction but not a resting place.

So a section may now declare the repository name that actually implements
it. The alias supplies *only which name to search under*: the state is
still computed from what that search finds, so an alias cannot promote a
row. One of the six declared lands on PARTIAL rather than
VERIFIED_CURRENT precisely because the module it names has no test.

An alias that stops resolving fails the compile rather than quietly
reverting its row to MISSING, and a section the repository already
answers under its own title is never redirected. Both are
mutation-verified, as is the dead-alias refusal.

Six reviewed mappings, each checked against the tree rather than inferred
from a filename: UNKNOWN-UNKNOWN MACHINE to Unknown-Unknown Mining,
FOUNDER-MINUTE ECONOMICS to founder-minute-priority, FRONTIER TECHNOLOGY
RADAR to Zero-Day Frontier Radar, PERSONAL KNOWLEDGE GRAPH to the Life
Knowledge Graph, RECURSIVE IMPROVEMENT VELOCITY to recursive-improvement
retention, FOUNDER ABSENCE TEST to founder-absence readiness.

253 MISSING -> 247, and 26 VERIFIED_CURRENT -> 31. The remainder still
needs per-section review; that is now a bounded review task rather than a
missing mechanism, and the blocker is reworded to say so.

commits.author: Claude
commits.message:
Build the top cut-set gap: a per-provider model failure map

The reconciler's highest-reference genuinely-absent section was CXLIX
MODEL FAILURE MAP -- nine other sections depend on knowing what a
specific provider gets wrong, and nothing in the tree modelled it. I
checked it was absent rather than renamed before building.

The router already scores candidates on aggregate quality and
reliability. An average is the wrong shape for the failure that matters:
a model that is excellent overall and reliably fabricates citations is
not a slightly-worse model, it is the wrong model for anything
citation-bearing and a fine one everywhere else. Averaged into one
reliability number that distinction disappears and the router keeps
choosing it for the one task class it cannot do.

So failures are recorded per provider x model x failure mode, over a
closed vocabulary -- an open one lets a caller invent a mode and attach
a penalty to it, which makes the map a way to express a preference about
a provider rather than a record of what it did. A mode becomes
SYSTEMATIC only on enough distinct non-self-reported observations: two
bad answers are an anecdote, identical observation ids collapse so
replay cannot manufacture a pattern, and a model's own account of its
mistake is evidence about the account. Penalties are bounded per mode
and in total, because an unbounded penalty is a blacklist by arithmetic.

Wired into routeModel as an optional input that subtracts rather than
disqualifies, and surfaced on the receipt so a route taken despite a
known weakness says so. Absent a map, routing is byte-identical to what
it was.

Mutation-verified: letting self-report count as independent, letting
replay accumulate, removing the penalty cap, ignoring task class,
reporting an OBSERVED mode as systematic, and removing the router
subtraction each fail the suite. The fifth of those initially survived
and exposed a real gap in my own test, which is now closed.

The reconciler independently re-measures the section as VERIFIED_CURRENT
on module, test and production-reachability evidence -- it was not told.

Also finishes the main repair: eight more rotted assertions rebound to
the invariants they had stopped describing. Two were wrong in a way
worth naming -- a sandwich-ordering test was matching import lines
instead of call sites, so two of its seven probes resolved to the top of
the file and the ordering it checked could never hold; and a git-pinning
assertion demanded a weaker form than the installer now uses, which
resolves the path through realpath.

Deterministic suite: 55 failures at session start -> 1, which requires a
clean working tree and passes once this is committed.

Handoff updated: active mission, the NULLSTAR reconciliation state, and
two new blockers (alias reconciliation, and the autonomy wake having no
schedule, which is a founder spend decision).

commits.author: Claude
commits.message:
Import PROJECT NULLSTAR and reconcile it against the organism

The founder delivered a 336-section directive in session. A session
transcript is not project memory, so it is imported per the chat-import
protocol as a durable human/machine pair with its truth class recorded:
FOUNDER_DIRECTIVE_IMPORTED / CHAT_SPEC_GOAL. Importing it records what
was asked for. It proves nothing implemented and grants no authority.

NULLSTAR is an internal codename for an execution-discipline program
beneath the existing hierarchy, not a new North Star. The Sovereign
Cognitive Continuum remains terminal; the Personal Civilization Engine
remains the contained life organism.

Section CCCVI asks for the thing this repository could not do: ingest a
new directive and say which of its requirements the organism already
satisfies. UberBond can compile coverage of its own canon, but a
directive arrives as prose under different names, and whichever model
reads it next has no way to tell a standing organ from an unmet
requirement. That is how a repository acquires a second capability
genome -- each one a sincere answer to a requirement already covered.

So the reconciler compiles a row per section and computes each state
from evidence, reusing the coverage matrix's locator and repo index
rather than growing a second view of the tree. Its discipline is the
matrix's: a name match alone never reaches VERIFIED_CURRENT, a boundary
or external gate cannot be satisfied by code, a milestone is blocked
until a receipt is supplied, a canonical concept lifts a row only as
high as that concept was independently rated, and a declaration may
excuse work but never claim it. Row count must equal section count.

It ranks unmet build targets by how often the rest of the corpus refers
to them -- a quantity read off the directive itself, recomputable and
arguable. It does not score them or estimate cost or unlock, because
sections CCCVII and CCCXIII name an underivable number as theater.

First run on this source: 25 VERIFIED_CURRENT, 29 PARTIAL, 14 BLOCKED,
14 NOT_CURRENTLY_JUSTIFIED, 254 MISSING. That MISSING count is an upper
bound and is reported as one: the matcher will not split a title on
whitespace, so a section the repository implements under a different
name reads unmet until a reviewed alias says otherwise. Understating
coverage is the safe direction and the number is honest about it.

Guards verified by mutation: allowing a source-only match to claim
VERIFIED_CURRENT, letting a boundary be satisfied by code, letting a
declaration claim completion, and dropping a section each fail the
suite.

Repair red main: three source defects and rotted test bindings

Current main was failing 55 deterministic tests. Diagnosis, in the two
classes the directive asks for:

SOURCE DEFECTS (the test was right, the tree was wrong)

- operational-world-resource-admission coerced absent permission
  collections with `?? []`, so a resource supplied with
  `permissions: null` on both sides admitted with ok:true and no
  permission evidence at all. An empty requested set has nothing to find
  unauthorized. Both collections must now be real arrays.
- Two callers of enforcement decisions sat outside the protected
  surface: sovereign-local-promotion calls validateAgentCodeChangeSet
  and sovereign-native-local-worker calls compileAgentCodeChangeSet.
  A caller that can discard the answer is a bypass whether or not the
  deciding module is touched.
- FIRST_CASH_OFFER.sku becomes requiresExactSku on the PayPal order a
  buyer approves, and nothing asserted it. Found because a mutation
  replacing it with a literal survived every declared suite.
- Four modules declared the canonical ZERO_EXTERNAL_EFFECTS name over a
  different eight-key shape. The dialect is real and is what persisted
  planning receipts contain, so it is now named once in effect-ledgers
  instead of being re-declared per module.
- Ten modules had landed with tests and no entry point or
  classification; they are recorded as NEEDS_TRIAGE with what is
  actually undecided about each.
- Five mutation anchors pointed at text that no longer exists, so five
  guards were silently untested. Re-anchored; two then survived, which
  is its own finding: CONV-07 named a suite that never asserted the SKU
  (test added), and CALIB-01 targeted one of two redundant integrity
  checks so the other absorbed it (retargeted at the verdict). All five
  now kill.

ROTTED BINDINGS (the tree was right, the assertion had stopped
describing it)

Test fixtures that had not kept up with tightened verifiers: the
state-evidence tribunal now requires VERIFIED_CURRENT rows to carry
evidence, the denominator requires an explicit concept/alias count, the
durable scheduler requires a settings store, and the first-cash
fulfilment runtime requires a bound prospect. Three Gmail adapter suites
used a fixture domain containing "uberbond", which the privacy firewall
correctly denied; the firewall is unchanged and the fixture is renamed.
Reason codes, truth-boundary wording and a schema version had drifted;
assertions now bind to the invariant rather than an inflection.

Two assertions were demanding something untrue and are replaced rather
than relaxed: the autonomy wake workflow has no cron in this source and
turning one on is a recurring spend the founder has not authorized, and
the handoff's runtime-proof blocker is genuinely closed, so requiring
its literal entry would invent a blocker.

The self-maintainer `|| true` guard now names the one place swallowing a
failure is correct -- teardown -- instead of banning the operator
outright, which is what made it fail the moment cleanup was added.

Also bounds the brain packet's mission line, which had pushed the
startup packet past its byte budget; the full text stays one documented
read away.

Deterministic suite: 55 failures -> the remainder in this commit's
scope; every repair above verified by running the suite it belongs to,
and the reason-code and denominator repairs verified by mutation.
